title: What a 'strong dollar' means for you

lines.text: When the news says the dollar is strong, it means one dollar buys more of other currencies.
Take a hundred euro hotel room. If one euro costs a dollar ten, you pay a hundred and ten dollars.
lines.say: Take a one hundred euro hotel room. If one euro costs a dollar ten, you pay one hundred and ten dollars.

lines.text: If a euro costs a dollar twenty-five, the same room costs a hundred and twenty-five. The stronger dollar saves you fifteen.
lines.say: If a euro costs a dollar twenty-five, the same room costs one hundred and twenty-five. The stronger dollar saves you fifteen.

lines.text: A strong dollar also makes imports cheaper for Americans. But it makes American products pricier for buyers abroad.

left.name: Wins
rows: Paying for things priced in euros

lines.text: That's why big U.S. companies often say a strong dollar hurt their overseas sales.
That's the money. See you at the next bell.
